passages.text: I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
Isaiah calls God his beloved.
Isaiah says, “I will sing a song for my beloved.”
This song is about my beloved’s vineyard.
My beloved owned a vineyard.
The vineyard stood on a very fertile hill.
passages.original: אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י לְכַרְמ֑וֹ כֶּ֛רֶם הָיָ֥ה לִֽידִידִ֖י בְּקֶ֥רֶן בֶּן־ שָֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: He dug it up and cleared the stones and planted the finest vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and dug out a winepress as well. He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, but the fruit it produced was sour!
passages.sermon:
God is the owner of the vineyard.
God prepared the vineyard carefully.
God dug the ground.
God removed the stones from the field.
God planted the best vines in the vineyard.
God built a watchtower in the middle of the vineyard.
God also dug a winepress in the vineyard.
God waited for the vineyard to produce good grapes.
The vineyard produced only sour fruit.
passages.original: וַֽיְעַזְּקֵ֣הוּ וַֽיְסַקְּלֵ֗הוּ וַיִּטָּעֵ֙הוּ֙ שֹׂרֵ֔ק וַיִּ֤בֶן מִגְדָּל֙ בְּתוֹכ֔וֹ וְגַם־ יֶ֖קֶב חָצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ וַיְקַ֛ו לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: “And now, O dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem and Judah.
God calls them to listen.
God asks them to judge.
God wants them to judge between Himself and His vineyard.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֛ה יוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֑ה שִׁפְטוּ־ נָ֕א בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין כַּרְמִֽי׃

passages.text: What more could I have done for My vineyard than I already did for it? Why, when I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is speaking.
The LORD cares for His vineyard.
The vineyard is the house of Israel.
The men of Judah are His chosen plant.
The LORD asks a question.
He says, “What more could I have done for My vineyard?”
He already did everything for it.
He did not leave anything undone.
He expected the vineyard to produce good grapes.
He asks, “Why did it produce only sour fruit?”
passages.original: מַה־ לַּעֲשׂ֥וֹת עוֹד֙ לְכַרְמִ֔י וְלֹ֥א עָשִׂ֖יתִי בּ֑וֹ מַדּ֧וּעַ קִוֵּ֛יתִי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem and Judah.
God calls Israel His vineyard.
God says, “Now I will tell you what I will do to My vineyard.
I will remove its hedge.
Fire will consume it.
I will break down its wall.
People will trample it.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ אוֹדִֽיעָה־ נָּ֣א אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה לְכַרְמִ֑י הָסֵ֤ר מְשׂוּכָּתוֹ֙ וְהָיָ֣ה לְבָעֵ֔ר פָּרֹ֥ץ גְּדֵר֖וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְמִרְמָֽס׃

passages.text: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and thorns and briers will grow up. I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks about His vineyard.
The vineyard is the house of Israel.
The LORD says, "I will make My vineyard a wasteland."
No one will prune it.
No one will cultivate it.
Thorns will grow there.
Briers will cover the ground.
I will command the clouds.
The clouds will not send rain on it.
passages.original: וַאֲשִׁיתֵ֣הוּ בָתָ֗ה לֹ֤א יִזָּמֵר֙ וְלֹ֣א יֵעָדֵ֔ר וְעָלָ֥ה שָׁמִ֖יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְעַ֤ל הֶעָבִים֙ אֲצַוֶּ֔ה מֵהַמְטִ֥יר עָלָ֖יו מָטָֽר׃

passages.text: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight. He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts owns a vineyard.
The house of Israel is this vineyard.
The men of Judah are the plant He loves.
The LORD looked for justice among them.
He saw bloodshed instead.
The LORD looked for righteousness among them.
He heard a cry of distress instead.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֶ֜רֶם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה נְטַ֖ע שַׁעֲשׁוּעָ֑יו וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel and Judah.
He warns those who add house to house.
He warns those who join field to field.
They keep adding land and property.
They do this until there is no space left.
They live alone in the land.
No one else remains near them.
passages.original: ה֗וֹי מַגִּיעֵ֥י בַ֙יִת֙ בְּבַ֔יִת שָׂדֶ֥ה בְשָׂדֶ֖ה יַקְרִ֑יבוּ עַ֚ד אֶ֣פֶס מָק֔וֹם וְהֽוּשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לְבַדְּכֶ֖ם בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: I heard the LORD of Hosts declare: “Surely many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts spoke to me.
I heard His words.
He said many houses will become empty.
These houses are large and beautiful.
No one will live in them.
passages.original: בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־ לֹ֞א בָּתִּ֤ים רַבִּים֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה יִֽהְי֔וּ גְּדֹלִ֥ים וְטוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks about judgment.
God says the land will not produce much.
Ten acres of vineyard will give only a small amount of wine.
A large amount of seed will give only a small amount of grain.
passages.original: כִּ֗י עֲשֶׂ֙רֶת֙ צִמְדֵּי־ כֶ֔רֶם יַעֲשׂ֖וּ בַּ֣ת אֶחָ֑ת וְזֶ֥רַע חֹ֖מֶר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֵיפָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks a warning.
He says, “Woe to those who rise early in the morning.
They chase after strong drink.
They stay up late into the evening.
Wine inflames them.
They seek pleasure in alcohol from morning until night.”
passages.original: ה֛וֹי מַשְׁכִּימֵ֥י בַבֹּ֖קֶר שֵׁכָ֣ר יִרְדֹּ֑פוּ מְאַחֲרֵ֣י בַנֶּ֔שֶׁף יַ֖יִן יַדְלִיקֵֽם׃

passages.text: At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see the work of His hands.
passages.sermon:
The people hold feasts.
They play the lyre and the harp at these feasts.
They use tambourines and flutes.
They drink wine.
They do not pay attention to what the LORD does.
They do not see the work of the LORD’s hands.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה כִנּ֜וֹר וָנֶ֗בֶל תֹּ֧ף וְחָלִ֛יל וָיַ֖יִן מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֨ת פֹּ֤עַל יְהוָה֙ לֹ֣א יַבִּ֔יטוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדָ֖יו לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding; their dignitaries are starving and their masses are parched with thirst.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people.
His people do not understand.
Because of this, God’s people will go into exile.
Their leaders will suffer hunger.
The people will suffer from thirst.
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן גָּלָ֥ה עַמִּ֖י מִבְּלִי־ דָ֑עַת וּכְבוֹדוֹ֙ מְתֵ֣י רָעָ֔ב וַהֲמוֹנ֖וֹ צִחֵ֥ה צָמָֽא׃

passages.text: Therefore Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws, and down go Zion’s nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers!
passages.sermon:
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Sheol opens its mouth wide.
Sheol has no limits.
The nobles of Zion go down into Sheol.
The crowds of Zion go down into Sheol.
The noise of Zion goes down into Sheol.
The revelers of Zion go down into Sheol.
The carousers of Zion go down into Sheol.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן הִרְחִ֤יבָה שְּׁאוֹל֙ נַפְשָׁ֔הּ וּפָעֲרָ֥ה פִ֖יהָ לִבְלִי־ חֹ֑ק וְיָרַ֨ד הֲדָרָ֧הּ וַהֲמוֹנָ֛הּ וּשְׁאוֹנָ֖הּ וְעָלֵ֥ז בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: So mankind will be brought low, and each man humbled; the arrogant will lower their eyes.
passages.sermon: God will bring down all people.\r\nGod will humble every person.\r\nProud people will lower their eyes.
passages.original: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל־ אִ֑ישׁ וְעֵינֵ֥י גְבֹהִ֖ים תִּשְׁפַּֽלְנָה׃

passages.text: But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
God is holy.
God will act with justice.
God will show His greatness through justice.
God will show He is holy by acting in righteousness.
passages.original: וַיִּגְבַּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְהָאֵל֙ הַקָּד֔וֹשׁ נִקְדָּ֖שׁ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃

passages.text: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures, and strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.
passages.sermon: Lambs will graze in their own pastures.\r\nStrangers will eat in the ruins of the wealthy.
passages.original: וְרָע֥וּ כְבָשִׂ֖ים כְּדָבְרָ֑ם וְחָרְב֥וֹת מֵחִ֖ים גָּרִ֥ים יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes, to those who say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come so that we may know it!”
passages.sermon:
God is the Holy One of Israel.
God is just and righteous.
Some people act with great deceit.
They pull iniquity with cords of lies.
They drag sin as if pulling it with cart ropes.
These people speak with arrogance.
They say, “Let God hurry and do His work.
Let us see what He will do.”
They say, “Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come quickly.
Let us know what will happen.”
God warns these people.
Woe to those who act in this way.
passages.original: ה֛וֹי מֹשְׁכֵ֥י הֶֽעָוֺ֖ן בְּחַבְלֵ֣י הַשָּׁ֑וְא וְכַעֲב֥וֹת הָעֲגָלָ֖ה חַטָּאָֽה׃ הָאֹמְרִ֗ים יְמַהֵ֧ר׀ יָחִ֛ישָׁה מַעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ לְמַ֣עַן נִרְאֶ֑ה וְתִקְרַ֣ב וְתָב֗וֹאָה עֲצַ֛ת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְנֵדָֽעָה׃ס

passages.text: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness to light and light to darkness, who replace bitter with sweet and sweet with bitter.
passages.sermon:
God warns certain people.
These people call evil things good.
They call good things evil.
They say darkness is light.
They say light is darkness.
They say bitter things are sweet.
They say sweet things are bitter.
passages.original: ה֣וֹי הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לָרַ֛ע ט֖וֹב וְלַטּ֣וֹב רָ֑ע שָׂמִ֨ים חֹ֤שֶׁךְ לְאוֹר֙ וְא֣וֹר לְחֹ֔שֶׁךְ שָׂמִ֥ים מַ֛ר לְמָת֖וֹק וּמָת֥וֹק לְמָֽר׃ס

passages.text: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.
passages.sermon:
God warns the people of Israel.
He speaks to those who think they are wise.
These people believe they are clever.
They trust their own understanding.
They see themselves as wise and intelligent.
God says, “Woe to them.”
passages.original: ה֖וֹי חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְנֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם נְבֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing beer, who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.
passages.sermon:
God warns the people of Israel.
He speaks against those who do wrong.
Some people are proud of drinking much wine.
Some people boast about mixing strong drinks.
These people are not heroes in good deeds.
They are only strong in drinking.
Some people let guilty people go free.
They do this because they receive bribes.
They take money to help the wicked.
They take away justice from innocent people.
They do not protect those who are right.
They make the innocent suffer.
God says woe to these people.
passages.original: ה֕וֹי גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים לִשְׁתּ֣וֹת יָ֑יִן וְאַנְשֵׁי־ חַ֖יִל לִמְסֹ֥ךְ שֵׁכָֽר׃ מַצְדִּיקֵ֥י רָשָׁ֖ע עֵ֣קֶב שֹׁ֑חַד וְצִדְקַ֥ת צַדִּיקִ֖ים יָסִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ס

passages.text: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God gave His people His instruction.
God is the Holy One of Israel.
The people rejected God's instruction.
The people despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
Because of this, God will judge them.
A tongue of fire quickly eats up straw.
Dry grass shrivels in a flame.
In the same way, their roots will rot.
Their blossoms will blow away like dust.
passages.original: לָכֵן֩ כֶּאֱכֹ֨ל קַ֜שׁ לְשׁ֣וֹן אֵ֗שׁ וַחֲשַׁ֤שׁ לֶֽהָבָה֙ יִרְפֶּ֔ה שָׁרְשָׁם֙ כַּמָּ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֔ה וּפִרְחָ֖ם כָּאָבָ֣ק יַעֲלֶ֑ה כִּ֣י מָאֲס֗וּ אֵ֚ת תּוֹרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְאֵ֛ת אִמְרַ֥ת קְדֽוֹשׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִאֵֽצוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore the anger of the LORD burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lay like refuse in the streets. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is angry with His people.
He raises His hand against them.
He strikes them down.
The mountains shake.
Corpses lie in the streets like garbage.
Even after all this, the LORD’s anger does not end.
His hand remains raised.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֡ן חָרָה֩ אַף־ יְהוָ֨ה בְּעַמּ֜וֹ וַיֵּ֣ט יָד֧וֹ עָלָ֣יו וַיַּכֵּ֗הוּ וַֽיִּרְגְּזוּ֙ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וַתְּהִ֧י נִבְלָתָ֛ם כַּסּוּחָ֖ה בְּקֶ֣רֶב חוּצ֑וֹת בְּכָל־ זֹאת֙ לֹא־ שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃

passages.text: He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold—how speedily and swiftly they come!
passages.sermon:
The LORD acts with power and authority.
He lifts a banner for nations far away.
He signals to people at the ends of the earth.
He whistles for them to come.
They respond quickly.
They come swiftly.
passages.original: וְנָֽשָׂא־ נֵ֤ס לַגּוֹיִם֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וְשָׁ֥רַק ל֖וֹ מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה מְהֵרָ֖ה קַ֥ל יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.
passages.sermon:
God calls distant nations to come quickly.
These people are strong and ready.
None of them grows tired.
None of them stumbles.
No one among them slumbers.
No one among them sleeps.
Every belt stays tight.
No sandal strap breaks.
passages.original: אֵין־ עָיֵ֤ף וְאֵין־ כּוֹשֵׁל֙ בּ֔וֹ לֹ֥א יָנ֖וּם וְלֹ֣א יִישָׁ֑ן וְלֹ֤א נִפְתַּח֙ אֵז֣וֹר חֲלָצָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א נִתַּ֖ק שְׂר֥וֹךְ נְעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.
passages.sermon:
God calls a distant nation to come quickly.
This nation is strong and ready for battle.
Their arrows are sharp.
All their bows are ready to shoot.
The hooves of their horses are as hard as flint.
The wheels of their chariots spin like a whirlwind.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִצָּיו֙ שְׁנוּנִ֔ים וְכָל־ קַשְּׁתֹתָ֖יו דְּרֻכ֑וֹת פַּרְס֤וֹת סוּסָיו֙ כַּצַּ֣ר נֶחְשָׁ֔בוּ וְגַלְגִּלָּ֖יו כַּסּוּפָֽה׃

passages.text: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away from deliverance.
passages.sermon:
They roar loudly.
Their roar is like a lion.
They roar like young lions.
They growl.
They grab their prey.
They carry the prey away.
No one can rescue the prey.
passages.original: שְׁאָגָ֥ה ל֖וֹ כַּלָּבִ֑יא וְשָׁאַג כַּכְּפִירִ֤ים וְיִנְהֹם֙ וְיֹאחֵ֣ז טֶ֔רֶף וְיַפְלִ֖יט וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃

passages.text: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.
passages.sermon:
On that day, a powerful army will attack the land.
They will roar over it.
Their roar will sound like the sea in a storm.
Anyone who looks across the land will see only darkness.
Distress will cover the land.
Even the light will grow dark under heavy clouds.
passages.original: וְיִנְהֹ֥ם עָלָ֛יו בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּנַהֲמַת־ יָ֑ם וְנִבַּ֤ט לָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וְהִנֵּה־ חֹ֔שֶׁךְ צַ֣ר וָא֔וֹר חָשַׁ֖ךְ בַּעֲרִיפֶֽיהָ׃פ
